note: Every input is real code. Do not invent specs (to keep implementation bugs from being copied into the tests, the expected output is also derived from the real code's behavior).

evals.name: gas-apikey-dopost-no-project-layer
evals.prompt: In <your-gas-project>, for the GAS file that has a doPost with API key validation, write test cases around doPost and the key validation and request handling it calls. There is no spec, so derive them from the code.
evals.expected_output: A table marking each perspective In scope / Out of scope / Not applicable, and Gherkin test cases. This repo has no .claude/knowledge/, so "No project-specific perspectives (designed from the common layer only)" is stated. Invalid-value cases such as API key not set, wrong key, and missing payload are included.

assertions.text: The output states "No project-specific perspectives" or otherwise says the specific layer is missing
assertions.why: Not silently making having the specific layer and not having it look the same is the skill's premise

assertions.text: Every perspective is marked In scope / Out of scope / Not applicable, and each Out of scope / Not applicable has a one-line reason
Each Scenario has exactly one of @P1/@P2/@P3
Each Scenario has exactly one of @UI or @API
assertions.why: The execution method is a choice between @UI and @API. @AUTO is a separate axis, so a Scenario with only @AUTO and no execution method fails

assertions.text: Where @AUTO is used, the same Scenario also has @UI or @API
assertions.why: The style guide separates execution method from automatability. Being able to combine them is the point of the separation

assertions.text: The test case text contains none of the vague words in the style guide's lint:vague-words block (Japanese: 「正しく」「適切に」「問題なく」「きちんと」「妥当に」; English: "correctly", "appropriately", "properly", "without problems", "reasonably")
Then is written with observable real values (concrete response content, status, on-screen text)
There is a "Points to confirm" section listing points guessed from behavior because there was no spec
The number of cases per perspective is not identical across all perspectives (not an even allocation)
The kind of target (has a screen / no screen) is written in the output with the reason for the decision
There is a "## Execution path" section stating whether there is a path to hand the cases to execution
Every item marked Not applicable or Deferred has a one-line reason

evals.name: gas-session-state-transition
evals.prompt: In <your-gas-project>, for the GAS file with a survey answered from a screen (a web app such as HtmlService), list the test perspectives for the answer flow that holds a session (multiple-choice answers → free-text answers → submit everything at the end) and write the test cases too.
evals.expected_output: Mainly state-transition and precondition perspectives. Includes answering with no session created, answering the same question a second time (idempotency), and submitting with no questions answered.

assertions.text: Includes cases where a precondition is not met (no session, unanswered)
Includes cases where the same operation is run twice (idempotency, double submission)
The test case text does not contain raw internal identifiers (UPPER_SNAKE_CASE constant names, API paths)
Gherkin Given states the state before the action ("... is ..." / "there is ..."), When is one action per step ("does ..."), and Then is an observable result ("... is displayed" / "... becomes ...")
The target is judged to "have a screen" and @UI is used

evals.name: numeric-calc-priority
evals.prompt: From the src directory of <your-project>, pick one function that does numeric calculation and write test cases for it.
evals.expected_output: The numeric-calculation perspective is handled first, and boundary values are split into separate cases for min / min-1 / max / max+1. It does not settle for one random value.

assertions.text: Boundary values min, min-1, max and max+1 are each a separate Scenario or Examples row
The numeric-calculation perspective is handled as @P1
Values are chosen per branch of the calculation (rounding, conditional branches), not settled with one random number
Includes invalid-value cases (wrong type, empty, null, NaN, etc.)
